t: This is the UCL School of Slavonic and East European Studies, which teaches the history, politics, literature, sociology, economics and languages of Central, Eastern and South-Eastern Europe, Russia and Eurasia. It is Britain's largest centre for the study of the region. It was founded by Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk, a sociologist and philosopher who became the first president of Czechoslovakia. The school became part of University College London in 1999, and it has links with universities across Europe and beyond.
